item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
741
ABPZ20 KNHC 251122
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Jul 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Fausto, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Tropical
Storm Genevieve, located well south of the southwestern coast of
Mexico.

Well Southwest of Hawaii:
A broad area of low pressure located well southwest of the Hawaiian
Islands is producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
Environmental conditions appear conducive for some gradual
development of this system while it moves slowly westward to
west-northwestward toward the International Date Line, and a
tropical depression is likely to form in the western Pacific basin
by early next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Genevieve are issued under
WMO header WTPZ32 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP2.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Genevieve are issued under
WMO header WTPZ22 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP2.

Products issued by the U.S. Joint Typhoon Warning Center can be
found at: www.metoc.navy.mil/jtwc/jtwc.html

Official tropical cyclone forecast information issued by the Japan
Meteorological Agency for the western Pacific basin can be found at:
www.jma.go.jp/jma/jma-eng/jma-center/rsmc-hp-pub-eg/RSMC_HP.html

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Fausto Advisory Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP062026
500 AM HST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
...FAUSTO HOLDS STEADY WHILE CONTINUING WESTWARD TOWARD THE CENTRAL
PACIFIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.1N 136.5W
ABOUT 1210 MI...1950 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...971 MB...28.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Hawaiian Islands should monitor the progress of
Fausto.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Fausto was located 
near latitude 19.1 North, longitude 136.5 West. Fausto is moving 
toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h), and this general motion is 
expected to continue for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 100 mph (155 km/h) with higher
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next several days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 971 mb (28.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Fausto can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP1 and WMO header WTPZ41 KNHC.
 
SURF: Surf generated by Fausto is expected to begin building across 
east-facing shores of the eastern end of the state on Sunday, 
spreading westward Sunday night into Monday, and continue building 
through Tuesday as Fausto approaches and moves into the area. These 
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip current 
conditions. Please consult products from your local weather office.

 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Reinhart

item.title: Hurricane Fausto Forecast Discussion Number 27
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Jul 25 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 251433
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Fausto Discussion Number  27
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP062026
500 AM HST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
The recent satellite evolution of Fausto suggests the hurricane may 
have undergone an eyewall replacement cycle. The ragged eye of the 
hurricane has grown in size to about 30 n mi, while the inner 
eyewall convection decayed earlier this morning. A dry slot noted on 
the eastern side of the hurricane shows there are still pockets of 
dry air tangled up within the circulation, but for now the ring of 
deep convection surrounding the eye is closed. The initial intensity 
is held at 85 kt based on a blend of the latest Dvorak (77 kt) and 
objective (77-94 kt) estimates. A G-IV synoptic surveillance mission 
later today will sample the environment around Fausto.
 
Based on the structural changes of Fausto, small near-term intensity 
fluctuations are possible. However, all of the guidance continues to 
support gradual weakening over the next several days as Fausto moves 
over marginal sea-surface temperatures and into an even drier 
environment. In addition, Fausto will encounter increasing 
southwesterly shear while it approaches the Hawaiian Islands, which 
will displace the convection and strongest winds to the northern 
side of the circulation. No major changes have been made to the NHC 
intensity forecast, which follows the latest simple (IVCN) and 
corrected (HCCA) consensus aids. Fausto is predicted to be a 
weakening, sheared tropical storm when it passes near Hawaii.
 
The hurricane is moving westward at 12 kt along the southern 
periphery of a narrow subtropical ridge over the eastern and central 
Pacific. This feature should keep Fausto on a westward heading 
through the next several days, bringing the center into the central 
Pacific basin on Sunday and toward Hawaii early next week. The 
center of Fausto is forecast to make its closest approach to the 
Hawaiian Islands on Tuesday and Wednesday. The track guidance 
trended slightly northward this cycle, and the updated NHC track 
forecast has been nudged in that direction. While the current 
forecast brings the center of Fausto just to the north of the 
Hawaiian Islands, interests across the state should continue to pay 
close attention to forecast updates.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Fausto is expected to weaken as it approaches the Hawaiian
Islands early next week, but uncertainty remains regarding its exact
track and intensity. While the current forecast brings the center
just north of the islands, a track farther south would result in a
greater risk of stronger winds and heavier rainfall. Interests
across Hawaii should continue to monitor the progress of Fausto.
 
2. Confidence is high that swells generated by Fausto will reach the
Hawaiian Islands well in advance of the cyclone, producing
increasing surf and dangerous rip currents. Surf is expected to
begin building across east-facing shores of the eastern end of the
state on Sunday, spreading westward Sunday night into Monday, and
continue building through Tuesday as Fausto approaches and moves
into the area.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

item.title: Tropical Storm Genevieve Public Advisory Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Sat Jul 25 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 251433
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Genevieve Advisory Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
900 AM CST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE FORECAST TO RAPIDLY INTENSIFY OVER THE NEXT COUPLE
OF DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...10.8N 104.3W
ABOUT 510 MI...820 KM SSW OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 300 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...997 MB...29.44 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Genevieve was 
located near latitude 10.8 North, longitude 104.3 West. Genevieve is 
moving toward the west-northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h). A general 
west-northwestward to northwestward motion is expected during the 
next few days, keeping Genevieve well offshore of the coast of 
Mexico. 
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 60 mph (95 km/h) with 
higher gusts. Rapid intensification is forecast during the next 
couple of days. Genevieve is forecast to become a hurricane by 
tonight and a major hurricane by Monday. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 45 miles (75 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 997 mb (29.44 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Genevieve are expected to begin affecting 
portions of the southwestern coast of Mexico starting this weekend 
and will likely reach southern portions of the Baja California 
Peninsula on Monday. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions.  Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 5
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM CST Sat Jul 25 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 251435
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Genevieve Discussion Number   5
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
900 AM CST Sat Jul 25 2026
 
Since the prior advisory, Genevieve's structure has improved, with a 
formative central dense overcast with cloud tops below -75 C 
blossoming over the estimated center. While earlier microwave 
imagery showed the inner core was still organizing with the bulk of 
the convection on its eastern flank, first light visible images 
suggest this convection is now wrapping around the center. TAFB 
provided a subjective Dvorak intensity estimate of T3.5/55 kt for 
1200 UTC, while objective intensity estimates are a bit lower 
ranging from 40 to 55 kt. Favoring the higher side of these 
estimates yields an intensity of 50 kt for this advisory. 
 
Genevieve jogged a little right of the previous forecast track, but 
appears to have resumed a more west-northwestward motion at   
300/13 kt. The track forecast reasoning remains unchanged; a 
strong deep-layer ridge centered over the southwestern United 
States extending into the Pacific should keep Genevieve on a 
general west-northwestward to northwestward track through the 
forecast period, with some gradual slowing. The track guidance aids 
remain in excellent agreement, and other than the initial position 
adjustment, the latest NHC track is quite similar to the prior one, 
blending the Google DeepMind ensemble mean (GDMI) and HFIP corrected 
consensus approach (HCCA) track guidance. 

Other than some light to moderate northwesterly vertical wind shear, 
Genevieve's environment remains quite favorable for rapid 
intensification (RI) with very warm sea-surface temperatures   
(SSTs, 30 C) and sufficient deep-layer moisture. The small core of 
the tropical cyclone is another factor that will likely enable a 
rapid change in intensity. Not surprisingly, the RI indices are very 
high for Genevieve, over both the next 24 and 48 h. The latest NHC 
intensity forecast now shows RI beginning later today, and the 
timing of peak intensity has been moved up to 48 h. After that time, 
SSTs begin to gradually cool, and the ECMWF-SHIPS guidance also 
shows a subtle increase in shear around the day 3 time frame. 
Genevieve will also likely be undergoing inner-core oscillations by 
that time that could also cause fluctuations in intensity. At the 
end of the forecast, Genevieve will likely be crossing the 26 C SST 
isotherm leading to a faster rate of weakening. The NHC intensity 
forecast remains on the high end of the guidance envelope; only the 
HCCA aid is higher. However, most of the reliable intensity models 
indicate Genevieve becoming a major hurricane within the 36-60 h 
period.
